newsitem.title: USA: Rio Grande Pipeline to begin deliveries soon - Amoco.
newsitem.headline: Rio Grande Pipeline to begin deliveries soon - Amoco.

text.p: Deliveries of liquified petroleum gas (LPG) into Northern Mexico from Amoco's Rio Grande LPG Pipeline and Supply project will begin within the next few weeks, said a spokesman for Amoco Corp said Thursday.
Robert Erikson of Amoco's liquids division did not give a specific date as to when the 220 mile pipeline that begins in West Texas will switch on, but said work on the joint venture is on schedule .

The Rio Grande joint venture pipeline is operated by MAPCO which also holds 45 percent ownership interest. Amoco Pipeline owns 30 percent with the remaining 25 percent held Navajo Pipeline, a subsidiary of Holly Corp.

The Rio Grande System joint venture was established in November 1995 to take advantage of the three to four percent annual growth rate of LPG demand in Northern Mexico, which traditionally has been supplied from the U.S. Gulf Coast through more expensive railcars.
"We believe the relevant market area for the project will continue to grow at similar rates in the future," Erikson told a U.S./International LPG Seminar here.

"Focus on (West Texas) and its proximity to Mexican export markets is tied directly to our business development strategy of linking international growth to our strong North American position," he added.
The primary staging point for volumes entering the system is Gaines County, Texas, about 14 miles east of Hobbs where Amoco has fractionator.
Erikson initial delivery capacity on the pipeline will be 24,000 barrels per day (bpd) of LPG, with expansion plans for up to 50,000 bpd.

The end of the line is at the Mendez Terminal, near Ciudad Juarez in Northern Mexico. The terminal and the 21.5 mile portion of the line inside Mexico are owned by and operated by Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), the Mexican state-owned oil and gas company.
